Transcript: Hello. I am Jonas and don’t really know what I’m supposed to say. I finished school, and since then I’ve basically done nothing. My parents think I’m depressed or something.
Hi Jonas. I am happy to have you here. Interesting, your parents think, you are depressed? How do they know this? What are you doing what they see as being depressed?

[shrugs] I guess they see me sleeping in, staying up late, not really going out much. They ask what my plans are, and I just say I don’t know. They get frustrated, I guess. It’s not like I’m sad all the time or anything. I just... don’t feel like doing much.
How do you feel about that?

I don’t know. It’s kind of annoying, I guess. They keep asking, and I don’t have an answer. It’s not like I *want* to just sit around all day. But every time I think about applying for something or looking into courses, I just... end up scrolling on my phone instead. It’s easier.

I understand that - these things can be quite exhausting and demanding. You say, you do not want to sit around. I guess, you are not sitting around all day, are you? Do you meet friends or something ales that is not applying or so?

Yeah, I mean, I do stuff. I play games with friends online sometimes, or we hang out. It’s not like I’m completely doing nothing. But it’s not... I don’t know, *productive* or whatever. And then I feel bad because my friends are all off doing their own things—uni, jobs, whatever—and I’m just here. [pauses] It’s not that I don’t *want* to do something. It’s just... hard to start.
Yeah, I see that. What is the difference between meeting with your friends to play games and the other stuff your parents want you to do?

[long pause] I guess with friends, it’s just... fun. No pressure. We’re just messing around, no one’s expecting anything from me. But the other stuff—applications, courses, all that—it feels like... if I pick the wrong thing, or if I mess it up, then what? At least with games, if I lose, it’s just a game. [shifts in seat] I don’t know, maybe that sounds stupid.

This does not sound stupid to me, actually. Let's make a thought experiment: Your parents seem to be dissatisfied with your current behavior and guess, when you come home today, they expect something to change and otherwise they will be dissatisfied again. What do you think would be the minimal thing to do, so that they have the feeling, that things are going into the right direction?

[sighs] I guess they’d want me to, like, apply for *something*. Even if it’s just one thing. But then I start looking, and there’s so many options, and I don’t even know what I’d be good at. [pauses] Maybe if I just... picked one random course or job and sent in an application, they’d back off for a bit. But what if it’s the wrong one? [looks down] I don’t want to waste time or money on something I’ll hate.
Yeah, it would be a waste of your life to do something, you hate, I see that. Let me ask you something: Do you play new games with your friend sometimes? Or always the same games?
We try new ones sometimes. Usually one of the guys finds something and we all check it out. If it’s bad, we just laugh and go back to the old ones. [shrugs] It’s not a big deal.
Well, if it is a bad game, you still have wasted your time, haven't you?

[quietly] Yeah, I guess. But it’s different. It’s just a game. If it’s bad, we move on. No one’s judging me for it. [pauses] With a course or a job... it’s like, if I pick wrong, it’s not just a waste of time. It’s like... a waste of *me*, you know? [looks away]
That is interesting! How would you realize that you have picked wrong?

[long pause] I don’t know. Maybe if I’m miserable every day. Or if I can’t keep up. Or if I realize I don’t actually care about it. [shifts in seat] But how am I supposed to know that *before* I start? It’s not like I can just... test it out like a game. [voice quieter] And what if I *do* pick something and then realize I’m bad at it? That’s worse, somehow.
Let's assume you performed a jon you have applied for - how would your parents realize that you are unhappy there?

[shrugs] I guess they’d notice if I came home stressed or complaining all the time. Or if I quit after a week. [pauses] But honestly, I’d probably just... not tell them. I’d say it’s fine, even if it wasn’t. I don’t like making them worry. [looks down] It’s easier to just... not talk about it.
Do you think that even without telling they might realize it anyway? I mean, we know how parents tick, they always see something?

[small, bitter laugh] Yeah, probably. They always seem to figure it out eventually. But by then, it’s already too late—I’d have wasted time, maybe money, and they’d be disappointed anyway. [pauses] It’s like... no matter what I do, I can’t really win. If I don’t try, they’re frustrated. If I try and fail, they’re still frustrated. [voice quieter] So why bother?
Let's assume, you liked the job you pick. What would make you realize that you picked correctly?

[long pause] I guess... if I didn’t dread going. If I actually looked forward to it, even a little. Or if I felt like I was getting better at something. [shrugs] But that’s the thing—I don’t even know what I’d *want* to look forward to. It’s not like I have some dream job or anything. [pauses] Maybe if it just... didn’t feel like a mistake. That’d be nice.
Yeah, I see that. Do you also propose games to your friends sometimes?

Yeah, sometimes. If I find something that looks cool, I’ll send it to the group chat. But it’s not a big deal if they don’t like it. We just pick something else. [pauses] It’s not like... a life decision or anything.
Would your parents see that you like the job you do?

[shrugs] Maybe. If I was actually happy, I guess they’d notice. But I don’t know if I’d even *tell* them. It’s weird—I don’t want them to be disappointed, but I also don’t want to, like, brag or whatever. [pauses] I’d probably just... not say much. They’d have to figure it out themselves.
Do or did you play games with your parents sometimes?

[small laugh] No, not really. My dad tried once—he’s terrible at them. It was kind of funny, but he got frustrated and gave up. [pauses] We don’t really do stuff like that. They’re more into... I don’t know, normal adult things. [shrugs] It’s fine.

Ah, these adults. It might sound strange, but I also do not understand them - playing games is so much fun. Actually, when I have to do stuff I do not like - I mean this stuff that you cannot avoid as an adult person - I try to make a game out of it.

[hesitant] Hmm. Like... how? [pauses] I mean, I guess that’s kind of smart. But I don’t know if I could do that. It’s hard to see applying for jobs as a game. [shifts in seat] It feels more like... a test I haven’t studied for.

Yeah, it's hard to make games out of this. I actually tought in a different direction: Your parents do not like to play games, but you do. So I guess, we will not make them easen up on you by playing games. But perhaps, you could do something, that you see as a game and they see it as you doing serious stuff.

[long pause] I don’t know... like, what? [thoughtful] Maybe if I treated applying like... a challenge or something. Like, "Okay, today I’ll just find *one* thing that doesn’t sound terrible." But then I’d probably just... not do it. [sighs] It’s hard to make it feel like a game when it doesn’t. [quietly] But I guess it’s worth a try.

Yeah, that would be a step that is too big. Something smaller. Perhaps like: you take the job offers and rate them as how much you think you might like them. And then you rate them as what you think your parrents would propose. And then you ask your parents to rate them how much you might like them. Then you take their list and your lists and compare it and see how good your estimate of them matches their rating and you see how much you actually concurr?

[stares blankly for a moment] That sounds... complicated. Like, a lot of work. And I don’t even know if my parents would do that. They’d probably just ask why I’m not applying to the "good" ones. [shifts uncomfortably] I mean, I get what you’re saying, but... it feels like another thing to mess up. [voice quieter] Maybe I’d rather just... keep things how they are.
Ok, this seems to be the wrong game then. So, how do you decide in the morning what you will do with your day?

[shrugs] I don’t really decide. I just... wake up, check my phone, see if anyone’s online. If not, I might watch something or play solo for a bit. [pauses] Sometimes I think, "Today’s the day I’ll actually look into stuff," but then... I don’t. [quietly] It’s easier to just... not think about it.
So let me ask you this: I heard that you are a bit annoyed by your parents sending you here and saying that you are depressed - did I hear that correctly?

[long pause] Yeah, I guess. It’s not that I’m *angry* or anything. It’s just... frustrating. They act like I’m broken or something. [sighs] I mean, maybe I *am* a little depressed, I don’t know. But it’s not like I’m sad all the time. I just... don’t know what to do with myself. [shrugs] And now I’m here, and I don’t even know what to say.
Ok. Let's assume you go home today and nothing changes - will that be fine, will you have to come here again?

[shrugs] I guess I’d have to come back. My parents would probably ask how it went, and if I say "fine" but nothing changes... yeah, they’d make me come again. [pauses] I don’t mind it, really. It’s not like I have anything better to do. [quietly] But I don’t know if it’s helping.
Ok, that sounds great. If you don't mind, then I think we shouldn't change anything now - it seems, that you need your time and we should have another meeting in two weeks. Would that be fine?

[long pause] Uh... sure, I guess. Two weeks is fine. [shifts in seat] It’s not like I have anything else going on. [quietly] But... I don’t know if just waiting will help. [pauses] Maybe I should try... something. Even if it’s small.

Ok, I have a wish: I will give a dice. Could you please roll it every morning? If it shows 1-3, it means that you will have a day of gaming, sitting around and all this stuff, just life as usual. If it shows 4-6, it means that this could actually be a day where something changes. Please observe any difference at this days and if you see something, write it down, just a short note, nothing complicated. Nothing has to happen, I am just curious about you life. Do you think you can do this for me?
[hesitant] Yeah, okay. I can try that. It’s just rolling a dice and writing stuff down. [pauses] But... what if I roll a 4-6 and then don’t do anything? [quietly] I don’t want to disappoint you.

Let's make it simple: Just write down the result of the roll for every day and if anything happens, you write it down, too. And if you do not write down any stuff besides the roll, then we assume nothing happend. We will learn something from that anyway, it's like an experiment where we do not know what we will find - I mean, that is, why we do experiments, right?

[small nod] Okay. Yeah, I can do that. It’s just... writing numbers and maybe some notes. [pauses] I guess it’s kind of like a game, in a way. [shrugs] I’ll try. But no promises if I forget a day or two.
Even that might be interesting! Yeah, kind of a little game, great. See you next time!
[stands up slowly] Yeah, see you. [pauses at the door] Thanks... I guess. [small, awkward smile] I’ll roll the dice.
